title: latency-backed-commit-tiers-with-precedence-fallbacks
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Background: Enterprise customers increasingly ask for both predictable throughput and strict latency guarantees for mission-critical inference endpoints. Existing reserve/burst packaging focuses on committed GPU credits and burst pools, but does not let customers purchase explicit latency SLOs at commit time. This ticket experiments with a new pricing construct: latency-backed commit tiers.

Goal: Design a packaging experiment that lets customers buy dedicated capacity with explicit p99 latency bands (and controlled headroom for autoscale/burst) and a precedence-based fallback/overflow model so we can guarantee latency while still offering efficient multiplexing for other customers. Produce contract language, pricing spreadsheet, mock quotes, and a light legal/SQ review checklist for initial pilots.

Proposal summary: Offer three latency-backed commit lanes: Gold (p99 <= 120ms), Silver (p99 <= 220ms), Bronze (best-effort). Customers commit a monthly reserved GPU-equivalent amount for a chosen lane. Pricing = base reserved price * lane multiplier (Gold x1.45, Silver x1.15, Bronze x1.0) + optional burst buffer credits. Each lane comes with documented autoscale headroom (minutes per hour) and a precedence score determining preemption order during congestion.

Precedence & fallback model:
- Gold lanes have highest precedence; on contention we preempt lower-precedence work (Silver/Bronze) to maintain Gold p99.
- Preemption is soft where possible: we offer a configurable warm-fail fallback to a qualified model variant (smaller quantized model) rather than dropping requests.
- Customers can opt into a 'surge-insurance' add-on that guarantees burst overage coverage at capped cost rather than preemption.

Billing & metrics:
- Billing base unit: reserved-GPU-hour at committed concurrency SLAs.
- Additional meter: latency-compliance credits (negative credits issued when p99 is missed; credits reduce future invoices or trigger SLA credits).
- Dashboards: per-route p99, headroom consumption, preemption incidents, warm-fallback activation rate.

Contract & enterprise-SQ implications:
- Need explicit SLA clause tying credits/credits-issuance to measured p99 on Redwood Console exports.
- Add auditability requirements for request routing decisions and preemption logs for security questionnaires.
- KMS/HSM and customer-managed model variants to be surfaced as options for Gold lane enterprise customers.

Pilot design: 6-8 strategic customers across AI-native startups and regulated enterprise teams. Run 8-week pilots with small discounts and telemetry gating (we collect p99, token throughput, headroom, preemption events). A/B test two defaults for burst pricing (flat buffer vs metered overage).
acceptance_criteria: Pricing spreadsheet with lane multipliers and cost model for committed units exists and passes Finance review
Legal-approved contract language for latency SLOs and credit remediation is drafted
Console dashboards instrumented to show lane-level p99, headroom, and preemption counts for pilot customers
Pilot onboarding runbook describing opt-in, telemetry exports, and rollback/fallback steps
Security questionnaire checklist updated with required artifacts (preemption logs, KMS usage, access controls)
decisions: Use reserved-GPU-hour as the billing primitive instead of tokens to keep pricing aligned with infra costs
Implement lane precedence as a deterministic score to simplify routing and audit trails
Default to warm-fallback (model-variant downgrade) before dropping requests to preserve UX unless customer opts out
Charge an explicit multiplier for latency guarantees rather than a hard per-request surcharge to make quotes predictable
